paper.title_en: Bayesian Inference of the Tip of the Red Giant Branch: I. One-Dimensional Analysis
paper.abstract_en: The tip of the red giant branch (TRGB) can be used as a relative distance measure as part of the cosmic distance ladder to infer the Hubble constant. We present a Bayesian framework for TRGB inference that incorporates selection effects and propagates per-star uncertainties, modelling the observed catalogue as a realisation of an inhomogeneous Poisson point process which includes the RGB and contamination from the asymptotic giant branch (AGB). We derive expressions for the predicted TRGB uncertainty in terms of the photometric noise, stellar density fainter than the tip, and the ratio of the AGB to AGB+RGB number densities, $r$. We validate these using synthetic data from a simplified luminosity function. Applying the full model to synthetic catalogues, we find that the dependence on $r$ is the strongest of the three, and that reliable inference requires $r \lesssim 0.5$; beyond this, the posterior is multimodal, and the TRGB cannot reliably be identified. We then fit data from 11 Hubble Space Telescope fields of the calibrator galaxy NGC 4258. We find intrinsic field-to-field scatter beyond measurement noise of $τ= 0.067^{+0.023}_{-0.017}$ mag, and a galaxy-level, extinction-corrected TRGB magnitude of $25.324 \pm 0.026$. Combining this with the maser distance to NGC 4258, we determine the absolute magnitude of the TRGB to be ${M}_{\rm{F814W}}^{\rm{TRGB}} = -4.073 \pm 0.026$ (tip) $ \pm$ $0.032$ (dist), consistent with, but brighter than, other recent analyses of the same data.
